findings.title: Per-user OAuth 2.0 code flow is documented for this app model
findings.detail: Dropbox uses OAuth 2.0 for app access to a user's data. The app constructs an authorization URL with client_id and redirect_uri and response_type=code, then exchanges the returned code at /oauth2/token using the client_secret.
findings.appliesWhen: Each customer account authorizes the app individually

evidence.quote: Dropbox uses OAuth 2.0
Construct a Dropbox authorization URL , with your application’s client_id and redirect_uri (if applicable) and specifying the response_type of code , and present it to the user
Call the /oauth2/token endpoint with your app’s client_secret to exchange the code for an access token in order to make API calls

findings.title: Register the app and configure exact redirect URIs before testing
findings.detail: Register the app in the Developer Console to obtain an app key and secret (client_id and client_secret) and add the exact redirect URIs under the OAuth 2 section of the Settings tab. Dropbox checks the redirect_uri at authorization time.

evidence.quote: Before you can get started, you’ll need to register your app with Dropbox by creating a new app in the Developer Console
for your application. Add them under Redirect URIs in the OAuth 2 section of the Settings tab. Dropbox checks that the specified redirect_uri parameter in your Authorization URL matches one
You’ll need to register the exact redirect URI(s) your app may use in the Developer Console

findings.title: Choose the App Folder access type at app creation
findings.detail: App Folder access limits the app's scope-permitted actions to data within the app folder only (/apps). This matches the requested boundary of no access outside the App Folder.
findings.appliesWhen: When creating the app as a scoped app

evidence.quote: App Folder: Your application will be able to take actions allowed by its scopes on data within its app folder only (in the /apps folder). This option is suitable for
App folder : Access limited to a single folder in the user’s Dropbox.
apps that export content or manage only their content.

findings.title: files.metadata.read covers listing folder entries and continuation
findings.detail: files.metadata.read is required for list_folder and list_folder/continue. Continue with the returned cursor while has_more is true to list all entries. The scope provides metadata access, so file contents are not downloaded or modified by this scope.
findings.appliesWhen: List file and folder names in the App Folder, including continuation

evidence.quote: Required scope: files.metadata.read Endpoint format: RPC
list_folder . Required scope: files.metadata.read

steps.title: Create scoped Dropbox app with App Folder access and register redirect URI
steps.detail: Developer creates a scoped app in the Dropbox Developer Console choosing App folder access, enables files.metadata.read on the Permissions tab, saves changes, and adds the exact redirect URI under OAuth 2 Redirect URIs. Record the app key (client_id) and app secret (client_secret) for the server only.
steps.doneWhen: App exists with App folder access, files.metadata.read enabled and saved, and the exact redirect URI registered.

fields: client_id: app key from Developer Console
client_secret: app secret, server-side only

steps.title: Open consent URL and verify redirect with code
steps.detail: Open the authorization URL in a browser as a test customer account, approve the app, and confirm the callback receives a code parameter and the expected state. Use the registered redirect_uri exactly.
steps.doneWhen: Browser is redirected to the registered redirect_uri with a code query parameter and matching state value.

evidence.quote: Construct a Dropbox authorization URL , with your application’s client_id and redirect_uri (if applicable) and specifying the response_type of code , and present it to the user

https://www.dropbox.com/oauth2/authorize?client_id=MY_CLIENT_ID&redirect_uri=MY_REDIRECT_URI&response_type=code Wait for the end user to complete authorization on dropbox.com, whom is then redirected back to your URI with an authorization code in the
You’ll need to register the exact redirect URI(s) your app may use in the Developer Console

fields: client_id: from app settings
redirect_uri: must exactly match registered URI
state: random value generated by the app
token_access_type: offline only if background refresh is needed

steps.title: Exchange authorization code for access token
steps.detail: Server calls the token endpoint with the returned code, client credentials and redirect_uri to obtain an access token. This is an unexecuted authorization step until a real code is obtained from the consent check.
steps.doneWhen: Token response contains access_token and expiry; no token is printed to logs.

evidence.quote: Call the /oauth2/token endpoint with your app’s client_secret to exchange the code for an access token in order to make API calls
Your application exchanges the authorization code for an access token that can be used to make secure calls to the Dropbox API (not shown)

When using refresh tokens, your call to the /oauth2/token endpoint with the grant_type of authorization_code will return a short-lived access token and a refresh token, which should be securely stored.

fields: grant_type: authorization_code (documented constant)
code: returned by the redirect
redirect_uri: same registered value
client_id and client_secret: app credentials

steps.detail: Call list_folder with empty path for the App Folder root, limited to names needed. Record entries and cursor. Use include_deleted false so only current entries return.
steps.doneWhen: Response returns HTTP 200 with entries containing .tag and name values and a cursor; has_more indicates whether to continue. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.
